title: Then We Shall Know: The Stunning Promise Hidden in Hosea 6:3 That Could Change the Way You See God Forever
paragraphs:
Then We Shall Know: The Stunning Promise Hidden in Hosea 6:3 That Could Change the Way You See God Forever
Why one ancient verse spoken to a broken nation still speaks directly into our deepest wounds, unanswered prayers, spiritual dryness, and desperate longing for God today.
There are moments in life when heaven feels silent.
Faith becomes memory instead of fire.
You still know the right words.
But somewhere deep inside, something feels distant.
Many believers quietly live in this place.
Not because they stopped loving God.
But because they stopped expecting Him.
And perhaps that is why Hosea 6:3 strikes the human heart with such unexpected force.
Because it was spoken into a moment very much like ours.
A moment when God's people desperately needed to know whether restoration was still possible.
"Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the LORD: His going forth is prepared as the morning; and He shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth." (Hosea 6:3)
At first glance, it sounds beautiful.
But beneath the surface lies a depth so profound that it can completely transform how we understand intimacy with God.
This is not merely a verse about knowing facts about God.
It is a verse about pursuit.
About the certainty of God's faithfulness toward those who continue seeking Him.
it is a verse about grace.
Because the entire book of Hosea is.
A wife who repeatedly abandons her covenant.
A husband who continues pursuing her.
It is one of the most shocking stories in all Scripture.
Yet God intentionally designed it this way.
Because Hosea's marriage was never merely about Hosea.
The book reveals a painful truth.
We seek fulfillment in places that cannot satisfy.
To understand Hosea 6:3, we must first understand the Hebrew language behind it.

וְנֵדְעָה נִרְדְּפָה לָדַעַת אֶת־יְהוָה
(Ve-ned'ah nird'phah lada'at et-YHWH)
"Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD."
The phrase נִרְדְּפָה (nird'phah) carries the idea of pursuing, chasing, pressing after with determination.
The kind of pursuit that refuses to quit when answers do not come quickly.
The kind of pursuit that continues praying when circumstances seem unchanged.
The kind of pursuit that keeps seeking Christ when emotions fluctuate.
The kind of pursuit that says:
"I may not understand everything, but I refuse to stop pursuing the One who saved me."
This is where many believers misunderstand spiritual growth.
We often assume knowing God means accumulating information.
But biblical knowing goes far deeper.
The Hebrew word used here is יָדַע (yada).
One of the richest words in the entire Old Testament.
It is the same word used throughout Scripture to describe profound relational closeness.
Hosea is not inviting us merely to learn about God.
He is inviting us to know Him.
This pursuit is rewarded with a breathtaking promise.
"His going forth is prepared as the morning."
The imagery would have been instantly understood by ancient Israel.
No human being wakes up wondering whether the sun will rise.
God says His presence is like that.
You may not see Him yet.
You may be fighting secret battles no one else understands.
The promise is not that life will always be easy.
The promise is that God remains faithful.
Even when our emotions tell us otherwise.
Even when we feel spiritually exhausted.
His faithfulness does not depend on our feelings.
"He shall come unto us as the rain."
Again, Hosea chooses imagery that his audience immediately understood.
Ancient Israel depended entirely upon seasonal rains.
The text specifically mentions the former rain and the latter rain.
The former rain prepared the ground.
The latter rain matured the harvest.
Together they represented God's sustaining provision from beginning to end.
God does not simply start the work.
Centuries later, the Apostle Paul would echo this truth:
"He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion." (Philippians 1:6)
The God who starts the story is the God who completes it.
And nowhere is that more visible than at the cross.
When we read Hosea, we cannot help but see Jesus.
The One who purchases back what was lost.
The One who loves the unfaithful.
The One who restores the broken.
The One who welcomes prodigals home.
Every act of restoration anticipates the Gospel.
The deepest meaning of Hosea 6:3 is not simply that seekers find God.
The deepest meaning is that God first sought us.
That is the scandalous beauty of grace.
The cross is proof that God does not abandon broken people.
Perhaps that is why this verse continues speaking across thousands of years.
Because every generation knows what it means to wander.
And every generation desperately needs grace.
Maybe that describes you right now.
Maybe you've carried hidden guilt for years.
Maybe you've convinced yourself that you've wandered too far.
Press on to know the Lord.
Not because your pursuit is perfect.
The greatest tragedy would be reading these words and remaining unchanged.
The Gospel was never meant to be merely admired.
It was meant to be embraced.
What season are you in right now?
Are you waiting for the dawn?
Or pressing forward to know Him more deeply than ever before?
Your testimony may encourage someone else who is struggling to keep going.
Because sometimes the miracle begins when we realize we are not walking alone.
And perhaps the most beautiful truth hidden inside Hosea 6:3 is this:
The God you are seeking is already moving toward you.
The dawn is closer than your darkness wants you to believe.
